diagnosis.root_cause: Bounded review confirms unstable landmark visibility from the shipped camera and persistent underlit cemetery exposure; the complete-run contract also remains unqualified.

stop_conditions: Preserve the intact authored cemetery and native Godot baselines.
Do not schedule deferred dense-profile evidence debt.
Host/tester own runtime recapture and issue closure.

strategy.rationale: Rebase spatial framing and anchors to the native map, repair exposure in the presentation layer, and complete authoritative run/upgrade/retry lifecycle behavior.

code: Developer runs native Godot project/static checks for modified scripts and scenes, verifies preserved authored scene bindings, and confirms tester-only actions are release-guarded/unbound.
runtime: Host recaptures authored-cemetery, exposure, complete-run, Result/Retry, and preserved boot/project evidence with candidate-bound MCP probes.

Tester replays spawn, critical route, near-contact/after-departure, cardinal/perimeter, ordinary movement, collision, disappearance/occlusion, dense combat, two successful builds, Bellkeeper, Result, and clean Retry; closes only directly retestable active issues.
Tester verifies upgrade focus and truthful deltas on keyboard, mouse, and gamepad, plus fresh-run reset receipts and no runtime errors.
visual: Compare gameplay screenshots to the supplied cemetery reference at spawn, route, dense combat, and landmark views for high-angle framing, external depth, warm/cool exposure, readable silhouettes, escape lanes, and compact HUD.
Recapture state/time-distinct adjacent frames for movement, combat, level-up, boss, Result, and Retry, prioritizing failed camera and exposure cells.

done_when: The cemetery provides larger traversable scale or an explicit expand around native streets plus a coherent external world/external depth beyond the gameplay boundary.

The keeper post, mausoleum, cracked bell, and every central building/landmark remain visible from spawn, critical route, near-contact, after-departure, and cardinal/perimeter views during ordinary movement/movement replay.
Visible geometry and collision agree for player and enemies; no pass-through, landmark disappearance/occlusion, or camera hiding occurs.
A clear boundary/perimeter preserves bounded gameplay and escape lanes without proxy floors or copied authored meshes.
tasks.instructions: Repair the camera/world spatial root cause around preserved CemeteryGarden. Rebase spawn, objective, navigation, collision, camera framing, and bounded landmark sight-lane handling to native streets/building transforms. Provide larger traversable scale or expand the route and an external world/external depth beyond the collision perimeter. Exercise ordinary movement/movement replay around every side of the central building and perimeter, comparing landmarks before approach, near contact, and after departure for collision agreement, disappearance/occlusion, escape-lane readability, and spawn fairness. Keep the authored environment intact as one authoritative package and minimize proxy clutter.
tasks.title: Rebase cemetery camera and spatial integrity to the native map

done_when: Shipped gameplay preserves moonlit blue-violet shadows and warm lantern accents while lifting blue-green underexposure enough to read streets, enemies, pickups, hazards, and landmark silhouettes.
Exposure is readable at spawn, critical route, dense combat, and cardinal landmark views without flattening hostile telegraphs or lantern-vs-moon hierarchy.
No import failures, placeholder materials, runtime errors, or geometry corruption are introduced.
tasks.instructions: Tune WorldEnvironment, moon/key/fill lights, fog/post exposure, and directly related bindings to resolve the underlit blue-green defect while retaining the PRD's stylized night language and supplied reference's warm-versus-cool hierarchy. Keep the map package preserved and changes scoped to presentation; do not add decorative proxy families.
tasks.title: Restore moonlit cemetery exposure and landmark readability

done_when: A normal release run completes five escalating waves including an elite and Bellkeeper boss, then reaches a clear Result state with truthful summary statistics and victory/failure.

At least two distinct ordinary successful build shapes complete end-to-end with observable differences in attack pattern, area control, targeting, cadence, mobility, survivability, pickup economy, or risk/reward; failures or diagnostic setup do not count.

Level-up choices lead with authored weapon/upgrade silhouettes, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant deltas, omit unchanged/placeholder rows, and support keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus/selection.
Retry from Result resets health, XP, wave/director, enemies, upgrades, audio, pause ownership, and HUD with no stale actors or duplicate UI.

Automatic combat, XP pickup, upgrade transaction, weapon/build identity, wave pacing, boss victory, Result, and Retry are reachable through ordinary release inputs; tester setup hooks, if any, are receipt-checked and excluded from release exports.
tasks.instructions: Complete the authoritative run/lifecycle and upgrade presentation path for real release qualification. Repair title-to-gameplay, wave/director, XP and upgrade draft, Bellkeeper victory/failure, Result, and Retry transitions so two materially distinct builds can each succeed through the ordinary route. Ensure the upgrade draft meets the authored visual hierarchy and that Retry disposes/resets every gameplay and UI owner. Keep deterministic tester setup separate from ordinary progression and guarded out of release.
